primaryText: He might get sick tomorrow.
translation: He might get sick tomorrow.
context: A modal for the present with an eventive predicate and a future frame adverbial.
comment: The paper lists must, ought to, should, may and might alike; might stands for all.

primaryText: He might get sick now.
translation: He might get sick now.
context: A modal for the present with an eventive predicate and a present frame adverbial.
comment: Marked ?? in the paper: the event must fall within the present, which the semantics does not exclude.

primaryText: He might get sick yesterday.
translation: He might get sick yesterday.
context: A modal for the present with an eventive predicate and a past frame adverbial.

primaryText: He might be getting sick now.
translation: He might be getting sick now.
context: A modal for the present with a progressive, hence stative, predicate and a present frame adverbial.

primaryText: He might be getting sick yesterday.
translation: He might be getting sick yesterday.
context: A modal for the present with a progressive predicate and a past frame adverbial.

primaryText: He might be sick now.
translation: He might be sick now.
context: A modal for the present with a stative predicate and a present frame adverbial.
comment: Against Enç's shifting modals: the same modal is non-shifting here and shifting with tomorrow.

primaryText: He might be sick tomorrow.
translation: He might be sick tomorrow.
context: A modal for the present with a stative predicate and a future frame adverbial.

primaryText: He might be sick yesterday.
translation: He might be sick yesterday.
context: A modal for the present with a stative predicate and a past frame adverbial.

primaryText: He must have gotten sick yesterday.
translation: He must have gotten sick yesterday.
context: A modal for the past, the modal over the perfect, with an eventive predicate and a past frame adverbial.
comment: The paper lists must, ought to, should, may and might alike; must stands for all, since only the subjunctive-form modals also scope under the perfect, [34].

primaryText: He must have gotten sick tomorrow.
translation: He must have gotten sick tomorrow.
context: A modal for the past with an eventive predicate and a future frame adverbial.
comment: The paper sets aside the future perfect reading, as in 'he may have arrived by next week'. With might the perfect-over-modal scoping of [34] would rescue the sentence.

primaryText: He must have been sick yesterday.
translation: He must have been sick yesterday.
context: A modal for the past with a stative predicate and a past frame adverbial.

primaryText: He must have been sick tomorrow.
translation: He must have been sick tomorrow.
context: A modal for the past with a stative predicate and a future frame adverbial.

primaryText: He may have won yesterday.
translation: He may have won yesterday.
context: PRES(MAY(PERF(YESTERDAY(he win)))): the winning lies within an interval preceding the forward interval of the present and within yesterday.

primaryText: He may win yesterday.
translation: He may win yesterday.
context: PRES(MAY(YESTERDAY(he win))): the winning must lie within the intersection of the forward interval of the present with yesterday, the null interval.
comment: Derived in the paper's [32]: never true, hence deviant.

primaryText: He might have been available yesterday.
translation: He might have been available yesterday.
context: A modal that can scope under the perfect, on the counterfactual scoping, with a past frame adverbial.

primaryText: He might have been available next month.
translation: He might have been available next month.
context: The perfect over the modal: the reference interval starts at a past time and extends to the end of time, admitting a future frame adverbial.

primaryText: It might have been raining yesterday.
translation: It might have been raining yesterday.
context: The perfect over the modal with a past frame adverbial.

primaryText: It might have been raining now.
translation: It might have been raining now.
context: The perfect over the modal with a present frame adverbial.

primaryText: He must have been available yesterday.
translation: He must have been available yesterday.
context: Must only scopes over the perfect; a past frame adverbial.

primaryText: He must have been available next month.
translation: He must have been available next month.
context: Must only scopes over the perfect, whose reference interval precedes the present; a future frame adverbial.
comment: Only modals in the subjunctive form, might, would, should, ought to, scope under the perfect.

primaryText: It must have been raining yesterday.
translation: It must have been raining yesterday.
context: Must over the perfect with a past frame adverbial.

primaryText: It must have been raining now.
translation: It must have been raining now.
context: Must over the perfect with a present frame adverbial.

primaryText: He may win the game.
translation: He may win the game.
context: A modal for the present: the possibility is from the perspective of the present about the future, and the modality can be epistemic or metaphysical.

primaryText: He may have (already) won the game (# but he didn't).
translation: He may have (already) won the game (# but he didn't).
context: The epistemic reading of a modal for the past: the modal over the perfect, perspective the present, orientation past; the issue is settled and the speaker does not know which way.
comment: The continuation 'but he didn't' is infelicitous on this reading.

primaryText: At that point he might (still) have won the game but he didn't in the end.
translation: At that point he might (still) have won the game but he didn't in the end.
context: The counterfactual reading of a modal for the past: the perfect over the modal, perspective a past time, orientation that time's future; the modality is metaphysical.

primaryText: He may/might have the flu (now).
translation: He may/might have the flu (now).
context: A modal for the present with a stative predicate on the reading where reference is to the present: only epistemic, since whether he has the flu now is settled by the course of events.

primaryText: He may/might get the flu.
translation: He may/might get the flu.
context: A modal for the present with an eventive predicate: reference to the future, and a metaphysical as well as an epistemic reading.

primaryText: It hasn't been decided yet who he will meet with. He may see the dean. He may see the provost.
translation: It hasn't been decided yet who he will meet with. He may see the dean. He may see the provost.
context: In the context of [42a] 'He will meet with one senior administrator': the issue is asserted not to be settled, and the modals get a metaphysical interpretation.

primaryText: It has been decided who he will meet with but I don't know who it is. He may see the dean. He may see the provost.
translation: It has been decided who he will meet with but I don't know who it is. He may see the dean. He may see the provost.
context: In the context of [42a]: the issue is asserted to have been settled, so after the first sentence settledness is presupposed and the modals have an epistemic reading.
comment: Future instantiation is settled only when the context contains information to that effect.

primaryText: He already returned.
translation: He already returned.
context: Already directly on an eventive predicate.
comment: Marked ?* in the paper, between questionable and starred.

primaryText: He did not write us yet.
translation: He did not write us yet.
context: Yet directly on an eventive predicate.
comment: Marked ?* in the paper, between questionable and starred.

primaryText: He has already returned.
translation: He has already returned.
context: Already on the perfect of an eventive predicate, a property of times.

primaryText: He has not written us yet.
translation: He has not written us yet.
context: Yet on the perfect of an eventive predicate.

primaryText: He might have already returned.
translation: He might have already returned.
context: A modal for the past with already: MODAL(ALREADY(PERF(he return))), the adverb scoping between the modal and the perfect.
comment: The paper lists must, should, might and may alike. The evidence that the auxiliary have is a perfect, not a past tense.

primaryText: He might not have written us yet.
translation: He might not have written us yet.
context: A modal for the past with yet between the modal and the perfect.

primaryText: He might already return.
translation: He might already return.
context: A modal for the present with already on an eventive predicate: no perfect to satisfy the sortal restriction.

primaryText: He might not write us yet.
translation: He might not write us yet.
context: A modal for the present with yet on an eventive predicate.
comment: On a deontic construal of the modal yet is acceptable; the paper sets root modals aside.

primaryText: He might still win.
translation: He might still win.
context: PRES(STILL(MIGHT(he win))): still scopes over the possibility modal, presupposing that the possibility of his winning was a live option before.
comment: The temporal, not the concessive, reading of still.

primaryText: At that point he might still have won.
translation: At that point he might still have won.
context: PRES(PERF(STILL(MIGHT(he win)))): still scopes over the modal and under the perfect on the counterfactual reading.

primaryText: He may still win.
translation: He may still win.
context: STILL over MAY: presupposes the possibility was live and asserts it persists, consistent with possibilities decreasing over time.

primaryText: He may already win.
translation: He may already win.
context: ALREADY over MAY: presupposes the possibility was not live and asserts it has become so, inconsistent with possibilities decreasing over time; already cannot scope under the modal, since its complement is eventive.

primaryText: Er könnte (schon) gewonnen haben.
translation: He might have (already) won.
context: German mirrors semantic scope in the linear order of the modal and the perfect auxiliary: the modal over the perfect, the epistemic reading only.
comment: Schon requires MODAL > ALREADY > PERF, which this order allows.

primaryText: Er hätte schon gewinnen können.
translation: He might have already won.
context: The perfect over the modal with schon.

primaryText: Er hätte (noch) gewinnen können.
translation: He might (still) have won.
context: The perfect over the modal, the counterfactual reading only.
comment: Noch requires PERF > STILL > MODAL, which this order allows.

primaryText: Er könnte noch gewonnen haben.
translation: He might still have won.
context: The modal over the perfect with noch.
